Treasury Yield Curve Data Utilities

Source: R/data-utils.r
fetch_fred_series.Rd

Functions for downloading and processing U.S. Treasury yield curve data from FRED API.

Downloads U.S. Treasury yield data for specific maturities from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) API.

Usage

fetch_fred_series(
  series_id,
  api_key = NULL,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  retries = 3L,
  cache_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

series_id

Character. FRED series ID for the treasury yield (e.g., "DGS10" for 10-year).

api_key

Character. FRED API key. If NULL, will look for fred_api_key environment variable.

start_date

Date or character in "YYYY-MM-DD" format. The earliest date to include.

end_date

Date or character in "YYYY-MM-DD" format. The latest date to include.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print processing information.

retries

Integer. Number of attempts for the HTTP request. Transient failures and 5xx responses are retried with exponential backoff; a 4xx response (a bad key or series id) is not, since retrying cannot help.

cache_dir

Character. Directory in which to cache responses. If given, a request already on disk is read from there instead of being re-fetched. NULL (the default) disables caching.

Value

A data.frame with date and yield value columns.

Details

Requires a FRED API key which can be obtained free at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/api_key.html Set the environment variable fred_api_key or pass it directly to the function.

Cache files are keyed on the series id and the requested date range only. The API key is never part of the key and is never written to disk. A cache hit is served before the key is looked up, so a cached corpus can be replayed with no key configured at all.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Set your API key first
Sys.setenv(fred_api_key = "your_api_key_here")
yield_10y <- fetch_fred_series("DGS10", start_date = "2020-01-01")
head(yield_10y)
} # }
